Arc melting of high-purity elements (purity > 99.9% in weight percentage) in an Ar gas atmosphere yielded an ingot of the equiatomic CoCrFeNi alloy. The ingot was re-melted five times to ensure chemical homogeneity.
The ingot was homogenized at 1200 °C for 12 h in an Ar gas atmosphere and then quenched with water to room temperature.
After hot-rolling the sample to a thickness of 3 mm (50% reduction) at 1200 °C, then it was rolled at ambient temperature to a thickness of 1.8 mm (40% reduction).

The grains were plastically deformed and distorted by CR, resulting in a high density of local distortion and subgrain boundaries with a misorientation angle of 2 °–5 °. Additionally, as the CR strain increased, the fraction of subgrain boundaries increased ( Fig. 2 (f)).
As shown in Fig. 6 (b), nanotwins are formed in the 10% CR sample, whereas no twins are formed in the 10% room-temperature-rolled sample ( Fig. 6 (a)).
The SFPs of the CR samples were 1.2 × 10 −3 (10%), 2.8 × 10 −3 (20%), and 7.7 × 10 −3 (30%),
The densities of dislocations in the CR samples are 11.4 × 10 14 m −2 (10%), 18.8 × 10 14 m −2 (20%), and 45.1 × 10 14 m −2 (30%), respectively.

evidence.quote: the room-temperature tensile yield strength of the CoCrFeNi HEA was increased by ∼290% from 243 MPa (as-recrystallized) to 941.6 MPa (30% cryo-rolled), while maintaining a tensile elongation of 18%. This was ascribed to the dense distribution of dislocations, nanotwins, and SFs. The yield and UTS were further tuned to 869 and 936 MPa, respectively
